subject: computer-science
title: Data Representation: Stretch — Media
welcome_lead: How do bits become pictures, music and text? Let's find out.
meta_desc: GCSE Computer Science stretch adventure on characters, images and sound representation.
final_note: You now understand how all media is just bits in disguise.

concepts.def: Encoding covering most world scripts (e.g. UTF-8).
The smallest dot in a digital image.
Bits used per pixel; more bits = more colours.
Samples taken per second when recording sound.

walkthroughs.body_html: ASCII uses 7 bits per character, giving 128 codes. 'A' = 65, 'a' = 97. Unicode (e.g. UTF-8) extends this to cover emoji, Arabic, Chinese and more.

File size (bits) = width × height × colour depth.

Example: 100 × 100 image at 8-bit colour = 100 × 100 × 8 = 80,000 bits = 10,000 bytes.

Sound file size (bits) = sample rate × bit depth × seconds.

Higher sample rate = more accurate waveform but bigger file.
